Append-only record of decisions that shape cross-repo work. Newest first. Reversing a decision gets a **new entry** that supersedes the old one — don't edit history.

## D-015 · Adopted from external assessment: one production line, status-language rule, syphilis-template refinement

*2026-08-20.* An independent engineering assessment of the ecosystem and program (prepared from repository evidence; kept as a dated internal snapshot with the working notes, not as wiki content) was reviewed point by point. **Adopted:** (1) *One production line first* — modernization proceeds along a single reference application taken end to end (raw data → data manager → calibration → simset → extraction → published artifact), then extracted as the scaffold other applications migrate through; selection is on the [roadmap](roadmap.qmd). (2) *Status-language rule* — "shipped" is reserved for capabilities installed in their durable home, used through the supported path, and regression-guarded; the toy model is accordingly a verified spike until it lands as a package fixture. (3) *Refinement of D-004* — syphilis CI demonstrably assembles, validates, and promotes from release-pinned intermediates, but the raw-data→section stage had no recorded CI runs at audit time; raw-to-final automation precedes cloning the pattern (D-004's direction stands). (4) *Provenance manifest* — a generated, validated receipt per released artifact, first for the reference application. (5) The `populate_outcomes_array` UB fix moved from deferred to next: at `jheem-containers@9c846bf`, the container runtime hot-patches the function in production (`assignInNamespace`, `base/common/custom_simulation.R:122`). **Declined at current scale:** governance-as-precondition staging, multi-metric outcome scorecards, and the heavier wiki operating loop (chronological ingest logs, automated claim linting); the cheap parts — commit-pinned references, evidence labels, link checking — are adopted as conventions instead. The assessment also caught a stale wiki claim (`create.solver.metadata` had become exported), validating D-014's premise; the affected pages were corrected with a newly verified example.

## D-014 · Wiki style: quantify, don't characterize

*2026-08-20.* A fresh-reader audit (an external senior-SWE review of the wiki against the actual repos) found the wiki factually accurate but severity-blind: neutral phrases ("several very large files", "~18 applications") kept the tone polite while losing the information a newcomer — human or AI agent — needs to calibrate risk, and the first fresh reader built a materially wrong risk picture from the wiki alone. Decision: wiki pages carry severity as **verifiable numbers** (line counts, file counts, presence/absence of tests/CI/README), never as adjectives or blame; per-repo state lives in the practice-baseline table on the [roadmap](roadmap.qmd) and flips as work lands. Rationale: the wiki is the first-read substrate for new people and for agents, so a tidy surface that discourages digging reproduces the black-box problem the wiki exists to fix. Texture that can't be published kindly stays in personal working notes (per [D-013](#d-013-wiki-voice-neutral-and-audience-invariant-no-machine--or-person-specific-detail)), but its quantified shadow must appear on the wiki.

## D-013 · Wiki voice: neutral and audience-invariant; no machine- or person-specific detail

*2026-08-19.* Wiki content is written for any reader — a team member, a new student, an outside collaborator — not from any one contributor's vantage point. Concretely: no local disk paths, no personal-tooling inventory (agent context files, symlinks), no maintainer attribution in structural descriptions, and pre-program history framed by its status (exploratory vs. team-adopted) rather than narrated. Machine- and person-specific operational detail lives outside the wiki (per-repo files, personal notes); the private surface is deliberately kept at zero — if genuinely non-public material ever needs a home, that's a separate private repo, created then, not preemptively. Plain-language motivation lives on [The Program](program.qmd); the roadmap stays the technical tracker.

## D-012 · jheem2 version convention: releases on master, `.9000` dev suffix on dev

*2026-08-18.* Observed practice: versions are bumped manually on **master** in dedicated "Increment version number" commits (1.12.3 as of March 2026); dev's DESCRIPTION goes stale between releases (it read 1.11.1 for seven months). Decision: keep release bumps on master exactly as practiced, and have dev carry `<last-release>.9000` (currently `1.12.3.9000`) — the standard R dev-version convention — so any dev build is distinguishable from, and sorts above, the latest release. Recorded gaps for the roadmap, not blocking: no git tags, no NEWS.md/changelog, DESCRIPTION `Date` was never maintained; release identity currently reconstructable only from bump commits. Consumers pinning git refs (containers, CI) are unaffected.

## D-011 · Wiki lives in the CIPHER-Epi org — resolves D-010

*2026-08-18.* The wiki repo is hosted at `CIPHER-Epi/jheem-wiki` (team org), private for now. The GitHub Pages publish workflow is manual-trigger-only until the "wiki goes public" roadmap item; enabling Pages will require making the repo public (or a paid org plan). The broader platform org-ownership question (delivery-platform repos under `ncsizemore`) remains open and is tracked on the roadmap.

## D-010 · Wiki repo hosting namespace — **Resolved by D-011**

*2026-08-17.* The wiki (and the delivery-platform repos) currently live under the `ncsizemore` personal GitHub namespace. Whether to migrate to a team/org namespace is undecided and is coupled to the broader platform org-ownership question (bus-factor mitigation). Until decided, the wiki develops locally / under personal namespace; migration is a rename, not a rewrite, because content is plain markdown in git.

## D-009 · WIP discipline: ≤2 active tracks, no branch older than a week

*2026-08-17.* Long-lived branches drift and die — the archived Dec 2025 exploration accumulated on one that fell 74 commits behind `dev`. Rule: at most two modernization tracks active at once; every increment merges to `dev` (or lands in this wiki) within a session or two; no working branch lives past ~a week.

## D-008 · Toy fixture is the keystone artifact; spike it early

*2026-08-17.* A small, self-contained model specification plus trivial data manager that runs in seconds — no NAS, no multi-GB simsets. It is the shared foundation for the test suite, runnable `@examples`, vignettes, and onboarding. It carries real technical uncertainty (no minimal JHEEM model has ever existed), so it gets a time-boxed spike before anything is scheduled on top of it. Fallback if "truly trivial" proves hard: a pinned, shrunken real workspace (à la `jheem-container-minimal`).

## D-007 · Calibration observability: read-only monitor first, in-loop stop later

*2026-08-17.* Team wants likelihood-progress visibility, per-city mixing stats, and termination of non-mixing cities. `bayesian.simulations` already checkpoints chains (with acceptance counts) to cache directories — so phase 1 is a **read-only monitor** over those caches (traces, acceptance, R-hat/ESS via `posterior`/`coda`), which touches no science path and can ship immediately. Phase 2 — graceful stop via a sentinel file checked at cache writes — modifies the sampling loop and therefore waits until a regression net exists. Monitoring/diagnostics live **above** the engine (analysis layer), never welded into `CALIBRATION_main.R`.

## D-006 · Documentation split: in-repo for API, wiki for cross-repo

*2026-08-17.* jheem2 API documentation (roxygen with runnable `@examples`, vignettes, pkgdown site) lives in the jheem2 repo, versioned with the code and executed by CI. The wiki holds only cross-cutting knowledge (ecosystem map, runbooks, decisions, roadmap). Boundary rule: *changes with a commit → repo; spans repos or outlives commits → wiki.* Corollary: examples are written against the toy fixture and never `\dontrun{}`, so docs double as regression tests.

## D-005 · Wiki: markdown-in-git substrate, rendered site as the team surface

*2026-08-17.* Canonical content is markdown in a git repo; a Quarto-rendered static site (GitHub Pages; later `docs.jheem.org`) is what the team browses. Rejected: GitHub's built-in wiki (hidden secondary repo, no CI/PR review, weak search) and wiki products like Confluence/Notion (breaks the agent-maintained update loop, creates a second source of truth, vendor lock-in). Rationale: readers vastly outnumber writers; the read path gets a real website, the write path stays PR-reviewed plain text that both humans and AI agents can maintain.

## D-004 · Syphilis-manager CI is the data-manager template

*2026-08-17 (direction established by team earlier in 2026).* The syphilis manager's pipeline — immutable release-pinned raw data (`data-raw-v*`), parameterized `jheem2_ref`, hybrid local/CI section builds converging on one regression-gated merge workflow, explicit promotion — is the pattern for all data managers. Next graduates: census and surveillance managers (currently ride along as pre-built dependencies). Long-term: reduce serialized-R6 fragility with a format-versioned data representation.

## D-003 · Structural decomposition of jheem2 is deferred, not canceled

*2026-08-17.* The 5-package split proposed in the Dec 2025 analysis is postponed until after API curation and a real test suite exist. Skepticism recorded about the multi-repo endgame at current team size (coordination cost of 5 versioned packages vs. enforced internal layering in one). The dependency/cycle analysis itself remains valid input; re-verify against current `dev` before acting on it.

## D-002 · Mine the `refactor/extract-packages` branch; don't merge or rebase it

*2026-08-17.* The Dec 2025 refactor branch (jheem.core extraction, "Phase 1 Week 1") is 74+ commits behind `dev`; rebasing a ~5,600-insertion structural change is riskier than redoing it on a tested base. Salvage instead: the architecture/dependency analysis (archived here), the `validate.R` golden-fingerprint concept (seed of the future test suite), and the concrete bug discoveries in its ISSUES.md — unregistered S3 methods, load-time top-level code, tracked `.o` artifacts — which are fixable on `dev` today.

## D-001 · Test-first sequencing for all jheem2 structural work

*2026-08-17.* Characterization/golden-master tests + CI come **before** refactoring, extraction, or engine changes — not "after the architecture stabilizes" (the ordering an earlier exploratory plan chose; see the [archive](archive/index.qmd)). Interim net until in-package tests exist: the `jheem-containers` golden/perturbation suite, run against candidate jheem2 refs (the base image pins jheem2, so the container cascade can gate engine changes now).
